string-methods.label: Useful String Methods
string-methods.summary: Use string methods to normalize text with `strip()` and `lower()`, replace selected text, and split or join text using separators.

sc-1.title: Choose the lowercase method
sc-1.prompt: Which string method changes all letters in a string to lowercase?
sc-1.hint: Choose the method whose job is changing letter case.

help.concept: `.lower()` returns a lowercase version of a string.
help.hint_2: `.split()` and `.join()` work with text pieces and separators.

sc-2.title: Pick the method for outside spaces
sc-2.prompt: Which method removes spaces from the beginning and end of a string?
sc-2.hint: Choose the method that removes whitespace only from the outside edges.

help.hint_1: It does not remove spaces between words.
help.hint_2: `.replace()` swaps selected text rather than trimming the edges.

mc-1.title: Methods that return strings
mc-1.prompt: Choose all expressions that return a string.
mc-1.hint: Check whether each expression returns one string or a collection of pieces.

help.concept: `.lower()`, `.strip()`, and `.replace()` return strings, while `.split()` returns pieces in a list.
help.hint_1: A case change still produces a string.
help.hint_2: Splitting is different because it breaks one string into multiple elements.

mc-2.title: Good uses of split and join
mc-2.prompt: Choose all true statements about `split()` and `join()`.
mc-2.hint: `split()` breaks text apart; `join()` combines text pieces.

help.concept: The separator belongs to the split or join operation and determines where text is broken or inserted.

options.d: `join()` removes outside spaces from a string

dr-1.title: Order the cleanup steps
dr-1.prompt: Put these steps in order to clean a name, make it lowercase, and print it.
dr-1.hint: Store the text first, trim it second, lowercase the cleaned value third, then print.

help.concept: Each assignment uses the value produced by the previous string operation.
help.hint_1: The variable must exist before a method can be called on it.
help.hint_2: Printing belongs after the final transformed value is ready.

dr-2.title: Order split and join
dr-2.prompt: Arrange the code steps to turn "red-blue-green" into "red, blue, green".
dr-2.hint: Split on the old separator before joining with the new separator.

help.concept: Changing separators can be a two-step transformation: split into pieces, then join the same pieces with a different separator.
help.hint_2: The join step must happen after the split has produced pieces.

fb-1.title: Fill the method name
fb-1.prompt:
Choose the method name for the blank so outside spaces are removed.

```python
clean = text.___()
```
fb-1.hint: This method trims the beginning and end of the string.

help.hint_1: Do not choose a method for changing case.
help.hint_2: Do not choose a method that breaks text into pieces.

fb-2.title: Fill the separator
fb-2.prompt:
Choose the separator for the blank so the words are joined with one space.

```python
result = ___.join(words)
```
fb-2.hint: The string before `.join()` becomes the separator placed between pieces.

help.concept: `" ".join(words)` inserts one space between each string in `words`.
help.hint_1: A hyphen would produce hyphen-separated text.
help.hint_2: Choose the literal containing exactly one space.

sketch-1.title: Clean and normalize text with methods
sketch-1.bodyMarkdown:
A string method is an operation attached to a string value.

Two common cleanup methods are:

- `.strip()` — removes whitespace from the beginning and end;
- `.lower()` — returns a lowercase version of the text.

```python
name = "  Ada Lovelace  "
clean_name = name.strip().lower()
print(clean_name)
```

Output:

```text
ada lovelace
```

Methods return new values. The original string is not changed automatically.

```python
text = "  HELLO  "
clean = text.strip()
lowercase = clean.lower()
```

You can call methods one at a time or chain them when each result is a string.

sketch-2.title: Replace selected text
sketch-2.bodyMarkdown:
Use `.replace(old, new)` when you want a new string with selected text swapped for different text.

```python
message = "I like cats"
changed = message.replace("cats", "dogs")
print(changed)
```

Output:

```text
I like dogs
```

The original `message` still contains `"I like cats"` unless you assign the returned string back to that variable.

`replace()` can affect every matching occurrence:

```python
text = "cat cat"
print(text.replace("cat", "dog"))
```

Output:

```text
dog dog
```

The two arguments matter:

```text
replace(text_to_find, replacement_text)
```

sketch-3.title: Split text apart and join pieces together
sketch-3.bodyMarkdown:
`.split(separator)` breaks one string into pieces. `.join(...)` combines string pieces using a separator.

```python
colors = "red-blue-green"
parts = colors.split("-")
result = ", ".join(parts)

print(result)
```

Output:

```text
red, blue, green
```

The separators play opposite roles:

- `split("-")` removes each `-` boundary and creates pieces;
- `", ".join(parts)` places `, ` between those pieces.

You can combine cleanup with the same workflow:

```python
raw = " apple,banana,cherry "
clean = raw.strip()
parts = clean.split(",")
result = " | ".join(parts)

print(result)
```

Output:

```text
apple | banana | cherry
```

Use `split()` when one string needs to become pieces, and `join()` when pieces need to become one string again.
